baseline.disclaimer: This is an independent conceptual study and is not an official ESO instrument model.
baseline.snr_definition: Expected source electrons / sqrt(forecast variance) per extracted spectral sample: one detector-pixel-wide wavelength bin summed over 4 spatial extraction pixel(s) in each of 1 independently read channel(s), 4 physical pixels in all. Not per physical detector pixel.
baseline.validation: Synthetic only; no OOPAO or observational validation

field_descriptions.noise_mode: noisy: one seeded Poisson/read-noise draw; noiseless: expected counts with the same forecast variance (injection/recovery check)
field_descriptions.run_identity_sha256: SHA-256 of the configuration, noise mode and template record; replayable with `aophoton replay`
field_descriptions.template: Template source; a file is identified by the SHA-256 of its bytes, a synthetic template by its generator inputs; samples_sha256 covers the samples used
field_descriptions.median_snr_per_spectral_sample: Median over the band of snr_per_spectral_sample (see snr_definition)
field_descriptions.median_snr_per_pixel: Deprecated alias of median_snr_per_spectral_sample, kept for compatibility; it is not per physical detector pixel
field_descriptions.estimated_rv_uncertainty_m_s: Fisher 1-sigma forecast from the expected spectrum [m/s]
field_descriptions.recovery_bias_m_s: Recovered minus injected RV of this single realization [m/s]; not an ensemble bias

spectrum_csv_columns.wavelength_um: Geometric-centre wavelength of the detector pixel [um]
spectrum_csv_columns.expected_source_e: Expected source electrons per extracted spectral sample
spectrum_csv_columns.background_subtracted_noisy_e: Background-subtracted electrons of the single seeded noisy draw (Poisson source, dark and background; Gaussian read noise)
spectrum_csv_columns.variance_e2: Forecast variance per extracted spectral sample [e^2]: source, dark, background and read noise of every summed pixel
spectrum_csv_columns.snr_per_spectral_sample: Expected source electrons / sqrt(forecast variance) per extracted spectral sample: one detector-pixel-wide wavelength bin summed over 4 spatial extraction pixel(s) in each of 1 independently read channel(s), 4 physical pixels in all. Not per physical detector pixel.
spectrum_csv_columns.coupling: Feed coupling efficiency, interpolated from the optical wavelength nodes

conclusions: At zero jitter, increasing residual WFE from 0 to 500 nm changes mean SMF coupling from 0.699 to 0.020; wavefront quality sets the photon budget.
At 150 nm WFE, increasing per-axis jitter from 0 to 40 mas changes SMF coupling from 0.489 to 0.249; injection stability remains important even at fixed AO residual.

At 400 nm WFE / 10 mas jitter, replacing the SMF with a 15-port lantern changes forecast σRV from 12.96 to 8.74 m/s at baseline brightness, but from 403.15 to 502.00 m/s at 0.01 × brightness. Under the assumed insertion loss and extraction noise, detector costs can reverse the throughput advantage.
